stories.headline: Trumbull asks residents to weigh in on the region’s 2027–2055 transportation plan
stories.summary: The town posted Oct. 1 that MetroCOG and the Naugatuck Valley Council of Governments want public priorities for the Metropolitan Transportation Plan covering Greater Bridgeport and the Valley through 2055. The plan is the federally required long-range mobility blueprint and is rewritten every four years. Trumbull is sending residents to the regional comment site rather than announcing a new local project of its own.

stories.headline: Trump says $90 Medicare Part B payments are going to more than 20 million seniors
stories.summary: President Trump said his administration will immediately send one-time payments of $90 — “nearly $100” in his post — to more than 20 million Medicare Part B enrollees, about $2 billion drawn from the Medicare Improvement Fund. A White House fact sheet says most eligible people get a direct deposit in early October and the rest a mailed check; people whose premiums Medicaid already pays, or who owe an income-related surcharge, are left out. He cast the fund as a congressional slush fund and said the payments are separate from ObamaCare refund checks.

stories.headline: Three South Alabama students charged with threatening Trump before the Mobile rally
stories.summary: Three University of South Alabama students were arrested Friday and charged with threatening the president over social-media posts in the days before Trump’s rally at the Mitchell Center, Fox News reports, citing federal affidavits. Investigators found the posts in pre-event searches and used emergency disclosures plus campus police information to identify them. One post, according to the affidavits, told people they would remember the campus the way they remember Utah Valley University, where Charlie Kirk was killed. The rally went ahead Friday night.

stories.headline: DOJ asks appeals court to pull Minnesota judges off immigration cases after NYT comments
stories.summary: Attorney General Todd Blanche said the Justice Department filed a judicial-misconduct complaint with the Eighth Circuit against seven Minnesota federal judges who spoke to the New York Times about the habeas surge that followed Operation Metro Surge. The complaint names Bush appointee Patrick Schiltz and Clinton appointee John Tunheim and asks that they be ordered off Department of Homeland Security immigration cases, arguing they commented on pending enforcement while those cases were still live. The judiciary’s misconduct process cannot automatically disqualify a judge, and the circuit chief judge decides whether the complaint goes to a special committee.

stories.headline: ICE memo bans high-speed chases and tightens who can make a traffic stop
stories.summary: A Wednesday memo from ICE Enforcement and Removal Operations, obtained by the Associated Press, tells officers they are not authorized to chase a vehicle that refuses to pull over and should record the vehicle for later investigation instead. Only officers who finished one of five ICE training courses may drive a stop; others can ride along in support. Stop vehicles must have lights and sirens, and every officer on scene has to wear and activate a body camera. The guidance follows more than a dozen shootings during ICE vehicle stops since last year. ICE called the memo a reminder and said stops and arrests continue.

stories.headline: FBI’s first cyber Ten Most Wanted fugitive is back in the U.S. after a Venezuela capture
stories.summary: Anibal Alexander Canelon Aguirre, alleged Tren de Aragua figure known as Prometheus, pleaded not guilty Friday in Nebraska to four conspiracy counts in a multimillion-dollar ATM “jackpotting” scheme and will stay detained. FBI Director Kash Patel called him the first cyber fugitive ever put on the Ten Most Wanted list and the 10th from that list captured since Trump took office. Prosecutors say he wrote malware that forced ATMs to spit out cash for the gang. He was arrested in Venezuela last month and returned to face the charges.

stories.headline: DOJ says UCLA Law kept a racial thumb on the scale after the Harvard admissions ruling
stories.summary: The Justice Department told UCLA that its law school intentionally used race in admissions from 2023 on, in violation of Title VI and the Supreme Court’s Students for Fair Admissions decision. Civil Rights chief Harmeet Dhillon said the school ran a two-tier bar: white and Asian applicants with LSAT scores comparable to admitted Black and Hispanic applicants were rejected, and in 2024 and 2025 half of admitted Black applicants scored at or below the 90th percentile of admitted white applicants’ scores. UCLA Law denied the charge and said review is merit-based. DOJ wants a voluntary compliance agreement.

stories.headline: Former Rep. David Rivera sentenced to 10 years for secret Maduro-era Venezuela lobbying
stories.summary: A Miami federal judge sentenced former Republican congressman David Rivera to 10 years after a jury convicted him of failing to register as a foreign agent and conspiring to launder money for work tied to Nicolás Maduro’s government. Judge Melissa Damian said the millions came from the Maduro regime and that Rivera’s friends would not have excused the same deal with Havana. Witnesses included Trump’s secretary of state and Rep. Pete Sessions, who said they felt misled about a PDVSA-linked consulting contract. Rivera has been jailed since the May verdict, plans to appeal, and has sought a pardon. He still faces a related case in Washington.

stories.headline: Apple’s rumored homeOS is expected this month on the HomePad smart-home hub
stories.summary: 9to5Mac, citing Mark Gurman, says Apple plans to unveil the HomePad hub on Oct. 13 with a new operating system expected to be called homeOS. The default screen is built around photo slideshows and a clock, in the vein of StandBy on the iPhone Duo, with a swipe up to an app launcher. Built-in apps include Music, Podcasts, Photos, Weather, FaceTime, Notes, Calendar, Messages, and Reminders. Touch works, but the point of the system is Siri with personal context — songs, notes, and calendar items tied to the household — and there is no App Store, only widgets brought over from an iPhone.

stories.headline: Neuralink says 50,000 hours of brain recordings set a new cursor-control record
stories.summary: Neuralink’s Oct. 1 update says clinical-trial participants have streamed more than 50,000 hours of unlabeled neural data, and the company is finally training participant-specific encoders on those recordings instead of leaving them unused. Calibration that used to take about 55 minutes a week is down to about 10 minutes for some users. One person held the same decoder for five straight days at 10 bits per second, and another reached 11.32 bits per second, which Neuralink called a new brain-computer interface record. The median across participants is about 10 bits per second.

stories.headline: Starlink cuts the Mini dish to $149, a hundred dollars under the usual kit price
stories.summary: Starlink emailed customers Oct. 2 that the portable Mini kit is $149, down from the usual $249 and below the earlier $199 low. The dish is the travel, camping, boat, and RV terminal, and a service plan is still required. The note did not give plan prices or say when the hardware discount ends, and it warned that price and availability can vary. SpaceX had already restored a free Mini perk for top-tier subscribers in the U.S. and Canada in August.

stories.headline: LEGO shows two 2027 Ninjago spinners, including an evil Cole and a Lloyd-vs-Ras battle
stories.summary: LEGO unveiled the first 2027 Ninjago sets on Oct. 2: spinner battles due Jan. 1. Set 71873 Cole vs. Evil Cole is 58 pieces, with a spectral, mirrored-torso Cole opposite the usual ninja. Set 71875 Lloyd vs. Ras Spinner Battle is 153 pieces and includes a small dragon build. Both are ages 6+ and preview a good-versus-evil Dragon’s Fury storyline rather than another wave of the sets already on shelves this month.

stories.headline: Highway test: Jeep Recon EV went 160 miles, about 60 short of its EPA rating
stories.summary: Car and Driver’s highway range loop got 160 miles from the Jeep Recon Moab, the electric Trail Rated SUV Jeep launched this summer at $66,995 with a claimed 670 horsepower. The EPA figure for the 94 kWh pack is up to 222 miles, so the test came up more than 60 miles short, at about 1.7 miles per kilowatt-hour — near the bottom of more than 100 EVs in that same test. The related Wagoneer S, on the same STLA Large platform and battery, managed 280 miles. Electrek notes the Recon’s taller, less aerodynamic shape is built for trails, not interstate efficiency.

stories.headline: A year after his knee injury, Braelon Allen is taking the lead reps with Hall sidelined
stories.summary: With Breece Hall’s quad injury expected to keep the starter out Sunday in Chicago, third-year back Braelon Allen (No. 0) has been getting most of the running-back reps. Allen told the team site he has always prepared as the lead back, and he marked almost exactly one year since the MCL sprain that ended his 2025 season in Miami. The Wisconsin product is 22, listed at 6-foot-1 and 235 pounds, and had 10 carries for 40 yards in the Week 1 win at Tennessee plus nine more carries since. He said the competition with Hall and Isaiah Davis is real and friendly.
